properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): writing one deployment topology down (1 region, 2 zones, 8 design hosts, a synchronous standby in the second zone, ~1 TB of fast storage, ~10 TB of object storage) took ~23 calls, and the counts, zones and sizes still live in names and prose. The operate layer holds no quantity anywhere: DEPLOYED_TO {status}, INCLUDES {as_checksum}, REQUIRES_RESOURCE {criticality}, Environment {env_type, location}, Resource with no amount. A sibling of the deferred req:vocabulary-covers-materiel, for software operations rather than physical materiel
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-29, item I23 of art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29.

① OBSERVED (friction #28, 0.74.0): "Recording one deployment topology took ~23 calls: 2 environments, 1 release, deploy_to, operates_in, 4 resources, 10 require_resource, 4 governed_by, 1 review_relations. Instance counts, zones and sizes have no structured field, so they live in names and prose. Expected: a count and a placement on a deployment edge, or a bundle form." The owner had asked for the deployment's SHAPE (host count, standby placement, snapshot and cold-storage locations, sizing from ~520 bytes per fact) so the failover, commit and reload budgets rest on a written topology.

② PRECEDENT: searched ("deployment topology instances zones", "Resource quantity amount capacity") in both designs.
- req:vocabulary-covers-materiel (DEFERRED 2026-08-07): "WHAT CANNOT BE SAID TODAY: a consumable and its consumption rate; a spare and its provisioning quantity..." It is the physical-materiel sibling, and it names the same `Resource` trap.
- dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built (open).
- The settled operations scope, dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-design-in-operations-where-incidents-feed-the-design ("concept → operations").
- No prior record of deployment quantities.

③ CANDIDATES:
- (a) fields exist and were missed;
- (b) quantities belong on Constraints (budgets) and the designer used the wrong layer;
- (c) the operate layer has no quantities;
- (d) the cost is only call count, which the bundle-write idea owns.

④⑤ MEASURED, schema/operate.yaml and environment.yaml at 0.74.0:
- Release has status and unit_type.
- Environment has env_type and location (one string: "region, host, site").
- Resource has resource_type, provider, version, components, features and declared_in: dependency fields, no amount.
- DEPLOYED_TO has status. INCLUDES has as_checksum. REQUIRES_RESOURCE has criticality. OPERATES_IN has only Project→Environment.
- No count, zone, replica, capacity or size on any operate type or edge, so (a) is refuted.
- (b) is partial: a CONSTRAINS contribution can carry a size as a budget spend (the designer did use memory budgets), but not "how many of this run where". A contribution is a spend against a limit, not a placement.
- (d) is true but secondary: even as one bundled call, the numbers would still have no field.
So (c) holds.

⑥ CLASS: the operate layer was modelled as TOPOLOGY-ONLY (what ships, where it goes, what it needs), with no quantities. Quantities are what an operations design is made of: counts, placement diversity, capacity. The materiel requirement found the same absence for physical systems and was deferred. This report is the first software instance, and it lands on the same layer. It also explains the I10 single-point-of-failure finding: redundancy cannot be read because it cannot be written.

⑦⑧ OWED: nothing to pin until the shape is decided. It is open in dec:idea-a-component-says-how-many-copies-run-and-where, which also has to settle the materiel requirement's own open question (widen Resource, or add a type).

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether reflow2 should model deployment at this grain at all, versus pointing at an infrastructure-as-code artifact as the source of truth and reading counts from it. The artifact route keeps one fact in one place, and the owner's standard-tracking rules may prefer it.
